**Official National Weather Service forecasts for Denver International Airport (KDEN) call for a sunny day with a high near 93–94 °F, placing the 92–93 °F bin as the clear market favorite at 82.5 % implied probability.** 

This reflects a thermal ridge advecting warmer air over the Front Range, pushing temperatures 6–7 °F above the 87 °F daily normal. Model consensus (including NWS point forecasts and ECMWF) has remained stable, with minimal disagreement and no significant moisture or cloud cover to suppress the peak. Afternoon observations through midday showed steady warming under light northeast winds, supporting the mid-90s outcome while rendering 94–95 °F a plausible but lower-probability scenario at 17.5 %. Traders appear to weigh the official forecast heavily, consistent with historical resolution on verified KDEN readings, and upcoming afternoon updates from NWS will provide the final data points before market close.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Numerical weather prediction models from ECMWF and GFS currently converge on a daytime maximum near 21–23°C for Moscow on August 21 under a stable late-summer regime dominated by moderate Atlantic air masses.** This positions 22°C as the market favorite at 54% implied probability, with 21°C and 23°C as plausible alternatives given typical model spread and minor uncertainties in cloud cover or timing of any light showers.

August climatology supports this range, with Moscow’s average high declining from roughly 24°C early in the month toward 21–22°C by the third decade amid shortening daylight and cooling soil temperatures. Recent observations reinforce the outlook: August 19 recorded only 19°C (well below the monthly mean), while August 20 reached approximately 22°C, indicating no strong warming or cooling trend. Overcast or partly cloudy conditions expected on the 21st would further limit surface heating and suppress any brief spikes above 23°C.

Traders are therefore weighting the central forecast heavily while assigning modest probability to small deviations driven by mesoscale details such as exact frontal timing or localized clearing. Updated model runs and official Russian meteorological service guidance remain the key near-term catalysts that could shift these implied odds.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent official forecasts position 31–32°C as the most probable range for Tokyo’s highest temperature on August 22, 2026.** The Japan Meteorological Agency currently projects a high of 33°C under cloudy skies with scattered showers developing later in the day, while other models from the BBC and Met Office converge on 32°C amid thundery showers and light winds. These conditions introduce cloud cover and precipitation that limit solar heating and convective mixing, keeping daytime peaks from reaching the 34–36°C levels sometimes seen in clear, high-pressure August setups.

August climatology in Tokyo features average highs near 31–32°C with high humidity, but the specific steering pattern and moisture influx expected this weekend favor moderated maxima. The market-implied odds (31°C at 36.5%, 32°C at 25.5%) closely track this consensus, with lower probabilities assigned to 30°C or 33°C reflecting residual uncertainty in exact timing and intensity of showers. Updated model runs and JMA briefings over the next 24–48 hours will be the key catalysts likely to shift probabilities as the event approaches resolution.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 22 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent PAGASA outlooks for Metro Manila on August 22 project a daytime high near 32°C under the active southwest monsoon, with 60-70% rain chances that can suppress peaks through cloud cover and afternoon convection. AccuWeather and climatological data place typical August maxima at 30-32°C, with model consensus centering on that narrow band amid variable humidity above 80% and steering patterns that favor scattered showers. The tight 31°C versus 32°C market split reflects uncertainty over exact timing of any thunderstorm activity or brief clearing that could shift the observed maximum by one degree, while lower probabilities for 30°C or 33°C+ align with the low likelihood of significant deviations from monsoon norms two days out.
